jobs.name: port-serein-low-poly-v2
jobs.prompt:
Use case: style-transfer.
Asset type: LOW-POLY production art direction reference for a futuristic sci-fi RPG.
Input image 1 is the EDIT TARGET, an earlier screenshot-based concept. Revise this exact scene into a markedly simpler, genuinely LOW-POLY version that a small team could assemble from generated meshes and simple Blender-built modular parts.
Preserve the same camera, framing, aspect ratio, perspective, horizon, building locations, main silhouettes, natural landscape layout and daylight. Keep the original ground and major tree placement recognizable. Do not change the scene into an isometric view or create a collage.
The change must be unmistakable: simplify ALL man-made objects to low polygon geometry, broad planar faces, visibly faceted 8-sided cylinders, single-segment chamfered box corners, chunky structural beams, simplified doors and windows, and a very small set of repeated modules. Flat or deliberately controlled shading on the architecture. Materials are mostly plain matte colors with subtle large-scale tonal variation. NO photoreal texture, grunge, scratches, bolts, tiny cables, densely ribbed paneling, mechanical greebles, ornate railings or baked high-frequency detail. Collapse small details into one readable block or a dark painted rectangle. A typical small structure should read as a few dozen purposeful solid forms, not hundreds of tiny parts. Surface detail should never be needed to explain what an object is.
Keep a serious, inhabited, human-scale frontier sci-fi mood. Modern sunlight, soft ambient occlusion and clear cast shadows provide depth to simple geometry. Palette: warm ivory structural faces, dark slate recesses, muted teal panels, restrained ochre-orange markings. Retain legible large doors, shaded gathering spaces, strong silhouettes and functional machinery. People and vehicles must be simple low-poly forms with ordinary proportions.
Important: this is a practical game-art reference for low-poly assets, NOT a photoreal scene with a polygon filter. Do not add random triangulation to smooth sky or cover surfaces with decorative triangle patterns. Avoid voxel cubes, toy proportions, miniature diorama framing, outlines, excessive neon and blurry painterly treatment. No title, text captions, interface, watermark or border. Keep the environment close to the original game's rendering; priority is simplifying the added architecture and props.
Scene-specific changes: preserve the city's terraced seaside footprint, civic tower, harbor, transit route, open water and beach. Reduce the whole city to a family of simple stacked chamfered building blocks. Window bands are broad dark color strips, balconies thick slabs, pillars simple extrusions. The landmark tower is a tapered polygonal mass with a teal inset and just one simple mast. The round-topped civic building has clearly octagonal stacked floors. Transit is a clean repeated beam and pier kit. Harbor cranes have only 3 or 4 thick beams; boats and skimmers are angular low-poly hulls. Rooftop plants are a few simple foliage clumps. Remove most minor antennas, machinery and street clutter. Let the city still feel established and inviting through terraces, color and scale. Water can be simplified to broad blue shading with restrained reflections; preserve its shape and horizon.
